fields.features_heading: The Monthly Work, Handled by Rule
fields.features_subheading: Automated property management starts with the dates a lease already sets. Emergent turns each date into a rule you can read.
fields.feature_1:
Reads the software you already run

Connects to any property management software that has an API. Leases and balances sync in and updates sync back out, and each run writes a row your whole team can search.
fields.feature_2:
Urgency set by words you choose

Tags a repair request as an emergency when it mentions a leak, no heat, or a lockout, using a word list you control. Every other request joins the morning queue for vendors.
fields.feature_3:
One rent roll every workflow reads

Keeps the rent roll and the vendor list in a database you own. Late notices and renewal offers read one shared lease table, and a corrected end date fixes both of them at once.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that follow the on-call rotation

Sends a Slack direct message or an email to whoever is on call that night. When nobody acknowledges within 15 minutes, the next person on the rotation gets the alert.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap on the 1st of the month

Sends a reminder to every tenant on the same morning, whether you manage 40 doors or 4,000. The whole rent roll goes out in one pass, with no task cap to hit halfway through.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase, in your GitHub

Exports every rule and screen to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer on your team can read the late fee logic line by line before the first notice goes out.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Workflows Every Rental Portfolio Runs
fields.tab_content_1:
Night leaks go straight to the on-call tech

At 9:40 PM a tenant in unit 4B at 1180 Alder Street reports water under the kitchen sink. The word leak marks it as an emergency. Luis Bennett, the on-call tech, gets a Slack direct message with the photo and the tenant's permission to enter. Routine requests wait until morning.
fields.tab_content_2:
Late notices for unpaid rent, sent the 6th

Rent at Lakemont Rentals is due on the 1st, and every tenant gets a reminder three days before. After the grace period, the app checks each tenant's ledger. Anyone still carrying a balance on the 6th gets a late notice with the $75 fee the lease sets. Tenants who paid hear nothing more that month.
fields.tab_content_3:
Renewal offers out 90 days ahead of lease end

With 90 days left on a lease, the tenant gets a renewal offer at the rent the property manager approved: $1,560 for unit 2A, up from $1,500. A reminder follows at 60 days. A lease still unanswered at 45 days becomes a call task for Ellen Marsh, and every answer updates the lease record.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every inquiry gets the same showing times

Each inquiry on a vacant unit gets the same reply within five minutes, listing the open showing times. The app books the slot the lead picks and logs where they found the listing. On Monday, the leasing team sees inquiries and showings for each listed unit.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to put property management automation on your rent roll, one workflow at a time, tested before tenants see it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one workflow and its dates
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the work your leasing and maintenance team repeats each month: logging repair requests, chasing balances after the 1st, sending renewal offers, and answering listing inquiries. Automating property management pays off first where one job touches every unit.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the workflow that costs your team the most hours, such as rent follow-up. Write its rule with real numbers: the due date, the grace period your leases give, the late fee, and who approves a notice.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Export your rent roll with unit, tenant, lease dates, rent, and balance, or connect your property software through its API. Any unit missing a lease end date is flagged for you to fill in instead of guessed.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent what starts the run, what each step checks, and who gets the message. Emergent builds the workflow, its database tables, and a dashboard for your team, and you change any step later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Run last month's ledger and repair requests through the app before it contacts a single tenant. Compare each notice and each alert it would have sent with what your team sent, unit by unit, and correct the rule wherever the two differ.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Keep handling requests by hand for the first two weeks while the app logs what it would have done. Any automation in property management that messages tenants should match your team's choices before it runs alone, and you switch over once the logs agree.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Build the second workflow on the same rent roll. Renewal offers read the lease end dates you cleaned up for late notices. Property management marketing automation can start with listing replies, which need only the unit table and your showing calendar.

faq_plan.q: What is a property management system?
faq_plan.ref: What is a property management system?

prov.original: What is a property management system?

faq_plan.a: A property management system is software that centralizes the day-to-day operations of owning and renting residential property. At minimum, it handles advertising, tenant screening, leasing, rent collection, maintenance requests, and accounting. Its lease and ledger records are what property management automation reads.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up property management automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one workflow that repeats every month, such as late rent notices or renewal offers, and describe its trigger and its rule in plain English to Emergent's AI automation builder. It builds the workflow and the dashboard your team checks. Test it on 5 of your own units before it reaches a tenant.

faq_plan.q: What is the most used property management software?
faq_plan.ref: What is the most used property management software?

prov.original: What is the most used property management software?

faq_plan.a: AppFolio is a large one by its own count: its annual report lists 22,096 property management customers and 9.4 million units under management as of December 31, 2025. Compare that with the figures other vendors publish, and check whether the software offers an API, since every automation on top of it reads its records.

faq_plan.q: How should property management workflow automation handle after-hours emergencies?
faq_plan.a: Give emergencies their own path, separate from the routine queue. Decide which words count as an emergency, who is on call each night, and how long the app waits before trying the next name. Log each acknowledgment with a timestamp. The escalation chain is the same one incident response automation uses in IT, applied to burst pipes and lockouts.

faq_plan.q: What should automated property management leave to a person?
faq_plan.a: Leave the judgment calls to a person: waiving a late fee, choosing between two contractor quotes, or replying to a tenant complaint. The app gathers the facts and routes each case to the staff member who decides. Emergent builds that hand-off from your prompt, and you change who gets which case by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should property management marketing automation track for each listing?
faq_plan.a: Track 4 numbers per listing: where each lead came from, how fast they got a first reply, how many showings turned into applications, and how many days the unit sat empty. Compare listing sites on applications instead of raw inquiries, since a site that sends 40 inquiries and no applications costs you showing time.

faq_plan.q: How should a property manager review listing copy before it goes live?
faq_plan.a: Add a review stage between draft and publish. The leasing agent writes the description from the unit record, it waits as a draft until the property manager approves it, and a rejected draft goes back with a comment. That draft-to-publish loop is how a content approval workflow runs for a marketing team, and listing copy fits it unchanged.

faq_plan.q: What data should I clean up before adding automation in property management?
faq_plan.a: Clean the fields every rule reads. Each unit needs one row and each active lease an end date, and each tenant needs a working email and mobile number. Merge duplicate tenant records first, or the same person gets two late notices. Your data lives in a database you own, and one fix there reaches every workflow.

faq_plan.q: Is automating property management worth it for a 10-unit portfolio?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the work repeats on dates, because rent reminders and lease end dates come round for all 10 units whether you own 10 or 1,000. Start with those two, since each needs only the rent roll and an email address per tenant. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How do I hold property repairs over a set cost for the owner's sign-off?
faq_plan.a: Set a dollar limit per owner, such as $500. Hold any work order above it until that owner says yes. The app emails the owner the quote and photos, records the answer with a timestamp, and sends a reminder after 24 hours. It is a standard approval workflow with one exception you should write in: emergencies skip the wait.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Property Management Automation for Your Rentals'; hero 'Create property management automation that routes repair requests and sends rent notices on the dates your leases set.' covers the whole job (repairs, rent, renewals, leads).

intent.evidence: Top 10 are PM software vendors and 'what can you automate' explainers; the page shows four concrete builds (night leak, late notice on the 6th, 90-day renewals, listing replies) plus a 7-step how-to starting from the rent roll.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'rent roll', 'grace period', 'doors', 'permission to enter', 'call task for Ellen Marsh'; automation table variant ('Behavior at cap', 'task cap').

openers.evidence: Tabs open on a scene ('At 9:40 PM a tenant in unit 4B...', 'Rent at Lakemont Rentals is due on the 1st'); features open on verbs ('Connects to', 'Tags a repair request').

craft.evidence: Sentences carry one idea each; QC Q5/Q8 clean. Minor FAQ 9 phrasing logged as a note.

voice.evidence: 'A developer on your team can read the late fee logic line by line before the first notice goes out.' Reads operator-written; FAQ 9 wording noted.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to prompt-build, api-connect, database-owned, alerts (escalation 'next person on the rotation'), no-caps, code-export ('on paid plans'), free-start. Third-party facts sourced: Slack DM (docs.slack.dev quote), PMS definition (Hemlane quotes), AppFolio 22,096 customers and 9.4 million units: both quotes found verbatim in appf-20251231.htm (fetched with a declared user agent, 200). Image numbers match copy ($1,450/$75, 2A $1,500->$1,560 at 45 days).

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in headings (real estate workflow automation, hotel automation untouched); links to incident response automation, content approval workflow, approval workflow are on-sense.

faq.evidence: 10 items, 2 PAA verbatim + 8 written. Written questions phrased as searchers ('Is automating property management worth it for a 10-unit portfolio?'), at most one secondary each, all property-specific, no legal/financial advice, no third-party pricing, no duplicate intent; no answer ends on a link-only sentence. Hub link in item 2.
